paths.description: Homepage/category index: primary entry template, navigation, search, preferences, security, performance, accessibility, and mobile layout.
New-content listing: representative high-traffic results template and item discovery path.
Category listing: representative taxonomy/detail-list template with pagination.
Primary item handoff: followed a current item URL to its external media provider and inspected readiness/metadata without starting playback.
Mobile search state: opened search, entered a no-result query, and inspected feedback/focus.
Arabic locale: representative RTL/localized template for language, direction, logical layout, and overflow.
Unknown route: representative HTTP 404 and recovery experience.
Repeated mobile-menu interaction: ten open/close cycles with before/after heap snapshots.

findings.summary: The page does not respond to the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the default capture; the probe reports color-scheme: normal and no preference-specific retinting.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive the site’s transitions.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, CSS still contains pervasive 0.3s transitions and repeated menu interaction produced 11 active animations; there is no reduce override.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes non-essential transitions and animations.

findings.summary: Route and state changes swap abruptly.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no view-transition-name or @view-transition usage across the category, listing, and outbound detail journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigations and same-document transitions for menu/search state, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages use JS-style static chrome rather than declarative scroll-state cues.
findings.evidence: The 12,920px home page exposes a scroll-top control, but inspected CSS has no scroll-state container queries or declarative scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a declarative scroll progress/position affordance for the long catalogue.

findings.summary: Navigation does not visibly preserve or direct attention.
findings.evidence: Representative category/listing navigation has no directional transition, target highlight, or post-navigation attention cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained directional View Transitions or target highlighting so users can track where navigation moved them.

findings.summary: Modal UI is implemented as custom containers rather than platform primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover, and 0 details elements while the DOM/CSS contains custom language and report modal implementations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal report flows and popover for transient language/menu UI, preserving declarative light-dismiss and focus behavior.

findings.summary: Reusable card and navigation components depend only on viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no @container rules; the stylesheet uses global max-width media queries throughout.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable grids/cards containment and adapt them with size container queries, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Mobile targets and keyboard focus are inadequate.
findings.evidence: At 360px, 249 interactive elements measured below 24px in at least one dimension; Lighthouse failed target-size, and focused icon buttons commonly compute outline: none.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase controls to at least 24px with spacing (prefer 44px for primary touch controls) and add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Search and error recovery states are not actionable enough.
findings.evidence: A no-result live search rendered a blank result area, while a real 404 says “Something went wrong” and “try again later” rather than identifying a missing page or offering a direct retry/home action.
findings.suggestedFix: Render explicit empty-search messaging and distinguish 404/network/server states with relevant recovery controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 5.2s (performance 0.80), although the warm raw-CDP trace measured 0.854s with no blocking tasks; the cold result remains the safer user-facing signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image/content, reduce discovery delay, and validate with mobile field data and repeat cold Lighthouse runs.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions, creating avoidable shift risk.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 98 images without width/height attributes; Lighthouse failed unsized-images, even though this observed run recorded CLS 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio for every image so space is reserved before loading.

findings.summary: Resource delivery includes avoidable discovery and caching costs.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 718KB; Lighthouse reported cache savings and image-delivery issues. GTM took 1.25s, while 98 images lacked intrinsic dimensions and many lacked responsive candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Set durable immutable caching for versioned assets, preserve async/defer, and improve responsive image/LCP delivery.

findings.summary: Analytics ships substantial unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 67KiB unused JavaScript, all from the 157KB Google Tag Manager payload, with about 44% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics only with a justified consent/context trigger, or replace it with a smaller first-party measurement path.

findings.summary: Core controls lack accessible names and some images lack alternatives.
findings.evidence: The probe found 67 visible unnamed controls; Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, and image-alt, including search, menu, language, logo, and pin controls. The images primitive found 38 missing alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide explicit accessible names/labels, mark decorative images alt="", and name repeated pin controls with their item context.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and focus visibility are broken.
findings.evidence: The home page jumps from h1 to dozens of h4 elements; Lighthouse failed heading-order, and many icon buttons had outline: none when programmatically focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sequential headings and a consistent :focus-visible ring without removing native outlines unless replaced.

findings.summary: The viewport prevents zoom and the media journey lacks exposed captions.
findings.evidence: The viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and target-size. The reached player exposed video elements with no caption tracks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no, enlarge targets, and ensure linked media provides caption/subtitle equivalents.

findings.summary: Asset markup is not fully sound.
findings.evidence: Although doctype and UTF-8 are valid, all 98 images lack explicit dimensions and Lighthouse reports a low-resolution icon.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic image dimensions, responsive sources, and a suitably dense icon asset.

findings.summary: Third-party runtime code triggers deprecated API warnings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded three deprecation warnings from Cloudflare challenge code, including Shared Storage and persistent StorageType usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or reconfigure the third-party challenge script and verify DevTools deprecation reporting is clean.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint does not return a sitemap.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is reachable, canonical and 36 hreflang links exist, but /sitemap.xml redirects to /en/sitemap.xml which returns an HTML “Something went wrong” page instead of XML.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a successful XML sitemap at the advertised endpoint and keep robots, canonical, and hreflang URLs consistent.

findings.summary: Catalogue pages lack structured and social metadata.
findings.evidence: Home recon found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags despite representing a large categorised collection; the outbound player page supplies rich metadata only after leaving the origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/CollectionPage or ItemList JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata to public catalogue pages.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but header and cookie protections are weak.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff; cookies found four cookies without Secure, including redisulid, and SameSite=None analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and Secure/SameSite cookie attributes appropriate to each cookie.

findings.summary: Analytics and third-party collection run without visible choice.
findings.evidence: Trackers detected Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; the HAR attributes 588KB of 718KB to third-party origins and records analytics collection on load. No consent surface appeared in the initial screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise telemetry, defer non-essential analytics until valid consent where required, and document each third party and retention purpose.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are largely absent.
findings.evidence: No clickjacking defense, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors was present; Referrer-Policy is unsafe-url, which can disclose full paths to outbound sites.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy, and other app-appropriate isolation controls.

findings.summary: The app-like bookmark experience is not installable or offline-capable.
findings.evidence: A manifest link exists, but its JSON contains only icons, with no name, start_url, or display; there is no service-worker registration or controller.
findings.suggestedFix: Complete the manifest and add a small service worker with an offline fallback for catalogue/navigation shell pages.

findings.summary: Failure states conflate missing content with server errors.
findings.evidence: The test route correctly returned HTTP 404, but rendered “Something went wrong” and “try again later,” implying a transient server failure and offering no prominent contextual recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Render distinct 404, timeout, offline, and server-error states with home, back, and retry actions as appropriate.

findings.summary: Content links silently redirect to a different commercial origin.
findings.evidence: Opening a bookmark.xxx video URL immediately landed on slutr.com with a UTM campaign parameter; catalogue cards do not visibly identify this cross-origin handoff.
findings.suggestedFix: Label outbound destinations and open them predictably, keeping the user informed before transferring context to a third party.

findings.summary: Responsive image delivery is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Images are mostly WebP and not oversized, but 60 of 98 lack srcset, 98 lack dimensions, and 9 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, and lazy loading for below-fold thumbnails while keeping the LCP image eager.

findings.summary: Third-party code is disproportionate to the catalogue shell.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 588KB of 718KB transferred; GTM alone is 157KB and two known trackers run on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte budget, defer optional analytics, and remove integrations whose measured user value does not justify their cost.

taskList.title: Repair accessible names, focus, zoom, targets, headings, and captions
Deploy secure headers, cookie flags, privacy controls, and a safer referrer policy
Bring cold LCP into the good range and fix responsive image delivery
Make all motion preference-aware and add restrained navigation continuity
Replace custom overlays with semantic dialog/popover primitives
Fix empty/error states and disclose cross-origin content handoffs
Reduce analytics and third-party JavaScript cost
Complete the manifest and add an offline fallback
Adopt container queries for reusable catalogue components
Clean up image markup and third-party deprecations
